Oddtoe is an animation agency and working studio in Melbourne and Los Angeles. One team scopes the idea, assembles the right animators and runs the project from first sketch to final frame. You brief one studio, not twelve freelancers, and one producer owns the delivery date.

[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][dfd_delimiter delimiter_style="dfd-delimiter-with-icon" icon_size="30" delimiter_border_style="dotted" icon_fontawesome="fas fa-arrow-circle-down" show_icon="enable_icon" delim_line_color="#8224E31C" icon_color="#EEE6F6" icon_hover_color="#D4C9E0"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="35" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="35" screen_tablet_spacer_size="35" screen_mobile_spacer_size="35"][vc_single_image image="16126" img_size="large" alignment="center" css=""][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="35" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="35" screen_tablet_spacer_size="35" screen_mobile_spacer_size="35"][dfd_heading enable_delimiter="" style="style_02" heading_margin="margin-bottom:20px;" subtitle="The short version" title_font_options="tag:h2|font_size:70|line_height:64" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_size:38|line_height:32"]

What does an animation agency actually do?

[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_column_text css=""]

An animation agency turns a brief into finished animated work and manages everyone who touches it. Oddtoe scopes the idea, assembles the animators, directors and writers the job needs, and runs it end to end, so you brief one team instead of hiring and coordinating a dozen separate people.

Oddtoe is an experiential design and generative-AI animation studio based in Melbourne, creating projection, installation, and animated work for events, venues, and galleries.

[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="80" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="80" screen_tablet_spacer_size="80" screen_mobile_spacer_size="80"][dfd_heading enable_delimiter="" style="style_02" heading_margin="margin-bottom:20px;" subtitle="Two words, two different jobs" title_font_options="tag:h2|font_size:70|line_height:64" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_size:38|line_height:32"]

Agency or studio, and does the difference matter?

[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_column_text css=""]

A studio makes the frames. An agency handles the frames and also the people, the schedule and the client. Oddtoe runs as both, so you get studio craft with a single point of contact who owns the delivery date, instead of a group chat full of freelancers.

The distinction matters most when something goes wrong. A freelancer who gets sick is your problem to solve. A studio reassigns the work internally. An agency does the same, and also absorbs the scheduling, the client updates and the revision rounds that come with it.

It matters again when a brief needs more than one discipline. A piece that wants character design, a writer and a compositor is three separate hires if you are managing it yourself. Oddtoe casts those roles against the brief and carries the coordination, which is usually the part nobody budgets for.

It cuts both ways: for a single short piece in a style one person already owns, a freelancer is often the better buy. See character design or documentary animation for what the studio does directly.

[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="60" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="60" screen_tablet_spacer_size="60" screen_mobile_spacer_size="60"][dfd_button button_text="Start a project" buttom_link_src="url:https%3A%2F%2Fwww.oddtoe.com%2Fcontact-oddtoe%2F|||" style="style_6" background="#8a8f6a" hover_background="#4e5041" border="border-style:none;|border-radius:5px;" hover_border="border-style:none;|border-radius:5px;"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner el_class="dfd_col-tablet-12" width="1/3" offset="vc_col-lg-4 vc_col-md-2 vc_col-xs-1"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="40" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row][vc_column][vc_column_text]

Questions & Answers

animation agencies

[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][dfd_accordion style="style-3" active_section="1" font_size="18" tab_title_google_fonts="yes" tab_title_custom_fonts="font_family:Arvo%3Aregular%2Citalic%2C700%2C700italic|font_style:700%20bold%20regular%3A700%3Anormal" icon_size="14"][vc_tta_section title="How much does it cost to work with an animation agency?" tab_id="1685677784578-172f9372-59216fce-87a69a68-2eae"][vc_column_text css=""]

It depends on length, technique and how much original design the piece needs. A short generative loop and a fully character-designed series sit at very different ends. Oddtoe quotes per project after a short scoping conversation, so the number reflects your brief rather than a rate card you have to reverse-engineer.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="How do I choose the right animation agency?" tab_id="1685677784323-438be9dd-da0e6fce-87a69a68-2eae"][vc_column_text css=""]

Look at three things: whether the work on the reel resembles what you actually need, whether one person will own your project end to end, and whether they will tell you when an idea will not work. Ask who is doing the animating and how revisions are handled before you sign anything.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="What kinds of projects does an animation agency take on?" tab_id="1685677784395-526dd6ff-b9c26fce-87a69a68-2eae"][vc_column_text css=""]

For Oddtoe: television and film work, commercials, character design, comedy and story writing, and projection and experiential pieces. Some clients want a single fifteen-second spot, others want a whole world built. Both get scoped the same way, idea first and then the team to make it.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="Can an animation agency handle AI or generative animation?" tab_id="1685677784507-83427dcb-7a756fce-87a69a68-2eae"][vc_column_text css=""]

Yes, where the brief calls for it. Oddtoe treats AI as a tool in the pipeline and not a gimmick to sell. It speeds up iteration and opens looks hand-drawing cannot reach, while a human director still owns the taste. There is a fuller explanation on the generative AI animator page.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="I am an animator looking for representation. Is this the right page?" tab_id="1786584255290-781b75e9-21a0"][vc_column_text css=""]

No. This page is for people who want animation made. If you are an animator, character designer or writer looking for an agent, Oddtoe keeps a separate guide to the animation agents and talent firms worth approaching. Start there instead.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][/dfd_accordion][vc_raw_html][/vc_raw_html][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][dfd_button button_text="Brief us" buttom_link_src="url:https%3A%2F%2Fwww.oddtoe.com%2Fcontact-oddtoe%2F|||" style="style_6" background="#8a8f6a" hover_background="#4e5041" border="border-style:none;|border-radius:5px;" hover_border="border-style:none;|border-radius:5px;"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][/vc_column][vc_column width="1/4"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row][vc_column][vc_column_text]
[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row] [vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" dfd_enable_overlay="" dfd_row_config="full_width_content_paddings" el_id="pat-section-1"][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="40" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/3"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/3"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="40" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][dfd_heading enable_delimiter="" style="style_02" heading_margin="margin-bottom:20px;" subtitle="What actually gets made" title_font_options="tag:h2|font_size:70|line_height:64" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_size:38|line_height:32"]

What can an animation agency make for you?

[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_column_text css=""]

Television and film work, commercials, character design, comedy and story writing, projection and experiential pieces. Oddtoe scopes a fifteen-second spot and a built world the same way: the idea first, then the people to make it.

Each of those is a practice in its own right. Character design builds casts you can put a franchise around. Comedy and story writing is where the structure comes from. Prop and 3D making covers the physical and digital objects a production needs. projection takes the work off the screen and onto a building.

Where a brief calls for it the studio also works in generative AI, as one technique among several rather than the headline. There is a fuller account on the generative AI animator page.

Knowing who is doing good work is part of the job. The studio keeps a running guide to the animation conferences and festivals worth attending, and the industry still does much of its business at Annecy’s MIFA market.

[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/3"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row][vc_column][vc_column_text]
[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row] [vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" dfd_enable_overlay="" dfd_row_config="full_width_content_paddings" el_id="pat-section-2"][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="40" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/3"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/3"][dfd_heading enable_delimiter="" style="style_02" heading_margin="margin-bottom:20px;" subtitle="How to pick one" title_font_options="tag:h2|font_size:70|line_height:64" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_size:38|line_height:32"]

How do you choose an animation agency?

[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_column_text css=""]

Three tests. Does the reel resemble what you actually need, will one person own the project end to end, and will they tell you when an idea will not work? Ask who is doing the animating and how revisions are handled before signing.

The reel test catches the most common mismatch. Agencies show their best work, not their most typical. If the piece you love was made by somebody who has since left, nobody will mention it unless you ask.

The ownership test matters because animation runs long. If the person who understood the brief is not the person answering your email in week six, you will explain it all again. That is usually where a fixed quote starts growing.

The third test is the one people skip. If an agency agrees with everything you suggest, you are paying for hours rather than an opinion. I would rather tell you an idea will not work while there is still time to change it.

[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/3"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="40" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row][vc_column][vc_column_text]
[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row] [vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" css=".vc_custom_1691550358421{background-color: #26161f !important;}" el_id="pat-article-1"][vc_column width="1/6"][/vc_column][vc_column width="4/6"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="60" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="30" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][dfd_heading enable_delimiter="" style="style_02" heading_margin="margin-bottom:20px;" subtitle="Why one team beats twelve" title_font_options="tag:h2|font_size:70|line_height:64" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_size:38|line_height:32"]

One brief, one producer, one delivery date

[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="15" screen_mobile_spacer_size="19"][vc_column_text css=""]

The pitch for hiring freelancers directly is that it is cheaper, and on a single piece it often is. The cost that does not appear in the quote is coordination. Somebody has to hold the schedule, chase the files, keep the style consistent between two people who have never spoken, and decide what happens when the storyboard changes in week three. On a direct-hire job that somebody is you.

That is the part an agency absorbs. I take a brief, work out which disciplines it actually needs, and put a producer on it to carry the schedule and the revisions. You get one contact and one delivery date. Internally the job might touch a character designer, a writer, an animator and a compositor, and you never have to hold that org chart in your head.

The second thing an agency buys is casting. A freelancer works in the style they already have, and a studio in its house style. An agency picks the hands to suit the brief, which is how the same team delivers a broad comedy spot one month and a restrained documentary sequence the next.

None of that makes an agency the right answer every time. A fifteen-second loop in a style one illustrator already owns does not need a producer sitting on top of it. The rule I use is simple: the more disciplines a brief touches, and the longer it runs, the more the coordination is worth paying for.

There is also more work about than usual. Screen Australia’s Drama Report 2024/25 records a record $2.7 billion spent on drama production in Australia, up 43 per cent, with post, digital and visual effects work accounting for $762 million of it, up 33 per cent. When that much is in production the good animators are already busy, which is a practical reason to book a team rather than go looking for one.

Freelancer, studio or agency?

[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_column_text css=""]

The same animation can be bought three ways. This is what changes between them.

CriterionFreelancerStudioAnimation agency
Who you briefOne personA studio producerOne producer who assembles the team
Range of stylesThat person's styleThe studio's house styleCast to suit the brief
Who holds the scheduleYou doThe studioThe agency
If someone drops outYou find a replacementThe studio reassigns internallyThe agency reassigns internally
RevisionsNegotiated per roundScoped in the quoteScoped in the quote
Disciplines coveredOneWhatever is in-houseHired against the brief

So you want an…

Animation agency

[vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner el_class=”dfd_col-tablet-12″ width=”1/3″ offset=”vc_col-lg-4 vc_col-md-2 vc_col-xs-1″][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner el_class=”dfd_col-tablet-12″ width=”1/3″ dfd_column_responsive_enable=”dfd-column-responsive-enable” offset=”vc_col-lg-4 vc_col-md-8 vc_col-xs-10″ css=”.vc_custom_1507277465182{padding-right: 0px !important;padding-left: 0px !important;}” responsive_styles=”padding_left_tablet:20|padding_right_tablet:20″][vc_column_text css=””]

Updated August 2026

[/vc_column_text]

[vc_column_text css=””]

Oddtoe is an animation agency and working studio in Melbourne and Los Angeles. One team scopes the idea, assembles the right animators and runs the project from first sketch to final frame. You brief one studio, not twelve freelancers, and one producer owns the delivery date.

[/vc_column_text]

[vc_single_image image=”16126″ img_size=”large” alignment=”center” css=””]

The short version

What does an animation agency actually do?

[vc_column_text css=””]

An animation agency turns a brief into finished animated work and manages everyone who touches it. Oddtoe scopes the idea, assembles the animators, directors and writers the job needs, and runs it end to end, so you brief one team instead of hiring and coordinating a dozen separate people.

Oddtoe is an experiential design and generative-AI animation studio based in Melbourne, creating projection, installation, and animated work for events, venues, and galleries.

[/vc_column_text]

Two words, two different jobs

Agency or studio, and does the difference matter?

[vc_column_text css=””]

A studio makes the frames. An agency handles the frames and also the people, the schedule and the client. Oddtoe runs as both, so you get studio craft with a single point of contact who owns the delivery date, instead of a group chat full of freelancers.

The distinction matters most when something goes wrong. A freelancer who gets sick is your problem to solve. A studio reassigns the work internally. An agency does the same, and also absorbs the scheduling, the client updates and the revision rounds that come with it.

It matters again when a brief needs more than one discipline. A piece that wants character design, a writer and a compositor is three separate hires if you are managing it yourself. Oddtoe casts those roles against the brief and carries the coordination, which is usually the part nobody budgets for.

It cuts both ways: for a single short piece in a style one person already owns, a freelancer is often the better buy. See character design or documentary animation for what the studio does directly.

[/vc_column_text]

Start a projectStart a project
[/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner el_class=”dfd_col-tablet-12″ width=”1/3″ offset=”vc_col-lg-4 vc_col-md-2 vc_col-xs-1″][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner]
[/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row][vc_column][vc_column_text]
[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row]
[vc_row bg_check=”row-background-dark” dfd_enable_overlay=”” el_id=”pat-faq”][vc_column width=”1/4″][/vc_column][vc_column width=”1/2″]
[vc_column_text css=”” item_animation=”transition.fadeIn”]

Questions & Answers

animation agencies

[/vc_column_text]

[dfd_accordion style=”style-3″ active_section=”1″ font_size=”18″ tab_title_google_fonts=”yes” tab_title_custom_fonts=”font_family:Arvo%3Aregular%2Citalic%2C700%2C700italic|font_style:700%20bold%20regular%3A700%3Anormal” icon_size=”14″][vc_tta_section title=”How much does it cost to work with an animation agency?” tab_id=”1685677784578-172f9372-59216fce-87a69a68-2eae”][vc_column_text css=””]

It depends on length, technique and how much original design the piece needs. A short generative loop and a fully character-designed series sit at very different ends. Oddtoe quotes per project after a short scoping conversation, so the number reflects your brief rather than a rate card you have to reverse-engineer.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title=”How do I choose the right animation agency?” tab_id=”1685677784323-438be9dd-da0e6fce-87a69a68-2eae”][vc_column_text css=””]

Look at three things: whether the work on the reel resembles what you actually need, whether one person will own your project end to end, and whether they will tell you when an idea will not work. Ask who is doing the animating and how revisions are handled before you sign anything.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title=”What kinds of projects does an animation agency take on?” tab_id=”1685677784395-526dd6ff-b9c26fce-87a69a68-2eae”][vc_column_text css=””]

For Oddtoe: television and film work, commercials, character design, comedy and story writing, and projection and experiential pieces. Some clients want a single fifteen-second spot, others want a whole world built. Both get scoped the same way, idea first and then the team to make it.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title=”Can an animation agency handle AI or generative animation?” tab_id=”1685677784507-83427dcb-7a756fce-87a69a68-2eae”][vc_column_text css=””]

Yes, where the brief calls for it. Oddtoe treats AI as a tool in the pipeline and not a gimmick to sell. It speeds up iteration and opens looks hand-drawing cannot reach, while a human director still owns the taste. There is a fuller explanation on the generative AI animator page.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title=”I am an animator looking for representation. Is this the right page?” tab_id=”1786584255290-781b75e9-21a0″][vc_column_text css=””]

No. This page is for people who want animation made. If you are an animator, character designer or writer looking for an agent, Oddtoe keeps a separate guide to the animation agents and talent firms worth approaching. Start there instead.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][/dfd_accordion][vc_raw_html][/vc_raw_html]

What actually gets made

What can an animation agency make for you?

[vc_column_text css=””]

Television and film work, commercials, character design, comedy and story writing, projection and experiential pieces. Oddtoe scopes a fifteen-second spot and a built world the same way: the idea first, then the people to make it.

Each of those is a practice in its own right. Character design builds casts you can put a franchise around. Comedy and story writing is where the structure comes from. Prop and 3D making covers the physical and digital objects a production needs. projection takes the work off the screen and onto a building.

Where a brief calls for it the studio also works in generative AI, as one technique among several rather than the headline. There is a fuller account on the generative AI animator page.

Knowing who is doing good work is part of the job. The studio keeps a running guide to the animation conferences and festivals worth attending, and the industry still does much of its business at Annecy’s MIFA market.

[/vc_column_text]

[/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/3″][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][vc_column]
[/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row][vc_column][vc_column_text]
[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row]
[vc_row bg_check=”row-background-dark” dfd_enable_overlay=”” dfd_row_config=”full_width_content_paddings” el_id=”pat-section-2″][vc_column]
[vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/3″][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/3″]

How to pick one

How do you choose an animation agency?

[vc_column_text css=””]

Three tests. Does the reel resemble what you actually need, will one person own the project end to end, and will they tell you when an idea will not work? Ask who is doing the animating and how revisions are handled before signing.

The reel test catches the most common mismatch. Agencies show their best work, not their most typical. If the piece you love was made by somebody who has since left, nobody will mention it unless you ask.

The ownership test matters because animation runs long. If the person who understood the brief is not the person answering your email in week six, you will explain it all again. That is usually where a fixed quote starts growing.

The third test is the one people skip. If an agency agrees with everything you suggest, you are paying for hours rather than an opinion. I would rather tell you an idea will not work while there is still time to change it.

[/vc_column_text]

[/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/3″][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][vc_column]
[/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row][vc_column][vc_column_text]
[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row]
[vc_row bg_check=”row-background-dark” css=”.vc_custom_1691550358421{background-color: #26161f !important;}” el_id=”pat-article-1″][vc_column width=”1/6″][/vc_column][vc_column width=”4/6″]

Why one team beats twelve

One brief, one producer, one delivery date

[vc_column_text css=””]

The pitch for hiring freelancers directly is that it is cheaper, and on a single piece it often is. The cost that does not appear in the quote is coordination. Somebody has to hold the schedule, chase the files, keep the style consistent between two people who have never spoken, and decide what happens when the storyboard changes in week three. On a direct-hire job that somebody is you.

That is the part an agency absorbs. I take a brief, work out which disciplines it actually needs, and put a producer on it to carry the schedule and the revisions. You get one contact and one delivery date. Internally the job might touch a character designer, a writer, an animator and a compositor, and you never have to hold that org chart in your head.

The second thing an agency buys is casting. A freelancer works in the style they already have, and a studio in its house style. An agency picks the hands to suit the brief, which is how the same team delivers a broad comedy spot one month and a restrained documentary sequence the next.

None of that makes an agency the right answer every time. A fifteen-second loop in a style one illustrator already owns does not need a producer sitting on top of it. The rule I use is simple: the more disciplines a brief touches, and the longer it runs, the more the coordination is worth paying for.

There is also more work about than usual. Screen Australia’s Drama Report 2024/25 records a record $2.7 billion spent on drama production in Australia, up 43 per cent, with post, digital and visual effects work accounting for $762 million of it, up 33 per cent. When that much is in production the good animators are already busy, which is a practical reason to book a team rather than go looking for one.

[/vc_column_text]

Which one is your brief?

Freelancer, studio or agency?

The same animation can be bought three ways. This is what changes between them.
